rollback_evidence: G82 (XE-M029), measured on IOL XE 17.18.2 (router) in the GNS3 lab, task netops-20261119-639. The key is ipv4:<name> or ipv6:<name> of a named extended ACL. Rules are comma-separated '<seq> permit|deny <protocol> <source> <destination> [eq <port>]' entries of IP/IPv6, TCP, UDP or ICMP with the addresses any, host <address> or a CIDR prefix of the family; the device prints named ports and wildcard masks, Admin compares the canonical form. Lines: 'ip access-list extended NAME' with '<seq> permit ...' and 'no <seq>', 'ipv6 access-list NAME' with 'sequence <seq> permit ...' and 'no sequence <seq>'; a changed rule is removed and added again. An IPv4 ACL without rules stays configured, an IPv6 ACL without rules does not exist (it is created with a rule and removed by delete). The device refuses a second sequence number with the same rule body, so the profile does too. The safeguard is the revert timer of the interface profile (configure terminal revert timer, configure confirm); apply needs the approved expected_plan_sha256. An ACL that is attached to an interface is changed only with its rules kept non-empty; on an up interface the change needs endpoint_impact naming the key; a management interface, a protected interface or an ACL that is also used by a route-map, NAT, line or another feature is refused. The check account reads show ip access-lists NAME and show ipv6 access-list NAME.
